title: Experimental interface positions tested across lineages, on the sequence thread's MAFFT alignments
builds_on: sequences/alignments/*.json, written by the sequence-alignment agent in this same session (MAFFT v7.526 --localpair --maxiterate 1000, Ensembl release 116 canonical proteins plus NCBI and Daane 2021 Data S1 rows). This layer did not realign anything; it reads their columns.
bird_exclusion: Class Aves is this project's frozen holdout; no bird row appears in these alignments and none was added here, until the holdout exam runs.

method.step1: Interface positions come from the deposited coordinates (structures/binding.json), in the structure's reference UniProt numbering via RCSB's SIFTS alignment.
method.step2: The structure's own species row in the MAFFT alignment is checked against the PDB reference sequence. Identical sequences map 1:1; otherwise a pairwise alignment is composed and its identity is reported.
method.step3: The interface position becomes an alignment column, and every species' residue in that column is read off.
method.rule: A column separates gliders from non-gliders only when every glider residue differs from every non-glider residue, at least TWO INDEPENDENT gliding lineages carry the glider residue, and at least five non-gliders are scored. Lineages are counted as lineages: the nine Exocoetidae are one.
limits: Gap columns are gaps, not differences.
Rows the sequence thread marked as tblastn projections rather than annotated proteins are flagged and excluded from the separation test.
The structures are human (and one mouse) proteins; every fish, reptile, amphibian and insect residue is reached by a cross-species jump.
Interface membership is a 4.0 A heavy-atom cutoff in one deposited conformation.
